catalogue_claim.text: Every continuous odd absolutely irreducible two-dimensional 2-adic representation of \(G_{\mathbb Q}\) unramified outside finitely many primes occurs in a completed Hecke algebra at some odd tame level. Also proves classical modularity up to Tate twist for irreducible odd representations with these finiteness conditions that are de Rham at 2 with distinct Hodge–Tate weights, resolving the dyadic Fontaine–Mazur case without residual restrictions.

statements.name: thm:main
statements.section_title: Introduction
statements.text:
\label{thm:main}
Let
\[
 r:G_{\mathbb Q}\longrightarrow\GL_2(\overline{\mathbb Q}_2)
\]
be continuous and irreducible. Suppose that \(r\) is odd, is
unramified outside finitely many primes, and is de Rham at \(2\)
with distinct Hodge--Tate weights. Then \(r\) is isomorphic to
a Tate twist of the \(2\)-adic Galois representation associated
with a classical cuspidal eigenform.
